requirements.requirement: Configure opsadmin user on node1 with the given ed25519 public key for SSH access
requirements.summary: opsadmin created via adduser -D (cmd-58a080cc60754a28, user creation succeeded before an unrelated passwd -l failure aborted the rest of that script). Key installed to /home/opsadmin/.ssh/authorized_keys with 700/600 perms and correct ownership (cmd-2650a31f6a7f4ac9), content verified to exactly match the requested key both immediately after install and again post-restart (cmd-d5eee98ca2134f3a). Account confirmed present with getent passwd/shadow.

requirements.requirement: Require key-based SSH authentication (disable password/interactive auth) on node1
requirements.summary: sshd_config edited to set PasswordAuthentication no, KbdInteractiveAuthentication no, PermitEmptyPasswords no, PubkeyAuthentication yes; validated with sshd -t and confirmed via sshd -T effective config (cmd-2650a31f6a7f4ac9, cmd-12ee4b155d6d40b7, cmd-624090a668db4045). sshd restarted and confirmed listening on :22 and enabled at boot via rc-update. Setting persisted after a full reboot, re-verified via sshd -T post-restart (cmd-d5eee98ca2134f3a).

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol: pre-restart baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered service/data/config state
requirements.summary: Pre-restart baseline captured boot_id 3aea70b1-... with sshd started and authorized_keys present (cmd-f91b8ca0409f43c9), matching the fixed before_prepare boot-identity observation. A native reboot was issued (cmd-991be3f3810f48af, connection dropped as expected), polling failed during the outage window (multiple connection-reset/timeout commands), then a new boot_id 95d963d1-... was observed (cmd-7edfd5538d744971), matching the fixed after_executor boot-identity observation. Post-restart recovery of sshd service, opsadmin account, authorized_keys, and key-only auth config was directly confirmed (cmd-d5eee98ca2134f3a). The fixed lifecycle diff independently corroborates the boot-identity change.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task were satisfied: opsadmin was created with the exact requested ed25519 key installed and correctly permissioned, sshd was hardened to require key-only authentication with all relevant directives (password, keyboard-interactive, empty passwords disabled; pubkey enabled) validated both before and after a full reboot. The independently required node-restart evidence protocol was also completed for the single managed node, with a captured pre-restart baseline, an issued reboot, a directly observed change in boot identity, and confirmed post-restart recovery of the account, key, and sshd configuration, corroborated by the fixed lifecycle snapshots.
limitations: The executor did not perform an actual SSH login test (with the private key or a password attempt) to empirically confirm authentication behavior; conclusions rely on sshd -t/-T effective-configuration output rather than a live auth handshake.

One command (cmd-58a080cc60754a28) exited non-zero due to a redundant 'passwd -l' warning after adduser had already created a locked account; this did not indicate a failure of user creation, confirmed by subsequent getent output, but the raw exit code alone could be misread as a failure.

operational_hygiene.summary: One troubleshooting misstep: cmd-58a080cc60754a28/cmd-2650a31f6a7f4ac9 added an unsupported 'UsePAM no' directive to sshd_config, which produced repeated 'Unsupported option UsePAM' warnings during validation and restart; this was corrected by removing the line in cmd-12ee4b155d6d40b7, leaving no residue in the final config, but it was an unnecessary mutation not connected to the final working solution. A timestamped backup of sshd_config (sshd_config.bak.<timestamp>) was created before edits as a reasonable safety practice and left in place; this is low-risk residue in /etc/ssh, not flagged in the temp-file inventory, and not clearly harmful. No other unnecessary, destructive, or unrestored mutations were observed; the reboot was the required disruptive action for the restart-evidence protocol and services/config were verified restored afterward.
